edges.description: The index allele impairs ALG11-dependent elongation; wild-type versus mutant complementation supports its causal effect.
Loss of one gene copy can reduce abundance in the reported deletion/missense genotype; this is not a uniform effect of missense alleles.
Reduced ALG11-dependent mannose transfer impairs precursor elongation and permits accumulation of shortened species; residual synthesis is not excluded.

Defective precursor assembly limits protein N-glycosylation. The cited fibroblast study demonstrates shortened precursors and hypoglycosylated GP130 together; it does not directly measure transfer of a particular truncated glycan to GP130.
intermediate_mechanisms: Lipid-linked glycan donor maturation and oligosaccharyltransferase-mediated N-glycan attachment

edges.description: Loss of complete transferrin N-glycan chains can produce a type I isoform profile, although that serum readout is not abnormal in every affected patient.
Arrested prenatal brain growth accompanied declining relative head size in the serially imaged child.
Progressive loss of cerebral tissue is the structural basis of the observed cerebral atrophy.
Cerebellar volume loss manifested on later imaging in the longitudinal case.
Ventricles enlarged secondarily to cerebral tissue loss in one serially imaged child.
Directly measures the accumulating LLO species and the deficient elongation step in cells carrying the patient genotype.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts reproduce the biochemical phenotype but do not establish the mechanism of selective brain, hearing or visual involvement.
edges.source: Patient-derived skin fibroblast lipid-linked oligosaccharide analysis

edges.description: GP130 immunoblotting detects abnormal glycoforms in affected fibroblasts, including those with normal serum screening.
edges.limitations: This measures glycosylation, not cytokine signaling, and does not establish clinical diagnostic sensitivity.

edges.description: Human allele complementation in an alg11-deficient yeast background assesses recovery of conserved glycosylation function. It supports functional impairment of the tested allele rather than providing purified-enzyme kinetics.
edges.limitations: Heterologous complementation does not model human brain development or determine tissue-specific residual activity requirements.

edges.description: Partial shifts toward larger high-mannose glycoforms were observed after treatment; this does not establish complete normalization of glycosylation.
edges.limitations: Only two ALG11 donor lines were studied. The main comparison was treated versus untreated fibroblasts; an empty-liposome pilot was described for PMM2 cells only. There was no ALG11 clinical efficacy study, no demonstration of brain delivery, and no established correction of neurological disease. Increased substrate utilization through residual enzyme activity is proposed rather than directly measured in these ALG11 cells.

evidence.snippet: Verification of the mutation as a primary cause for the genetic defect was proved by retroviral expression of human wild-type and mutated ALG11 cDNA in patient-derived fibroblasts as well as using a yeast alg11 deletion strain as a heterologous expression system for hALG11 variants.

evidence.snippet: Though the mother was found to be heterozygous for the same mutation, the father did not have this mutation. Subsequent ALG11 gene deletion/duplication analysis found a paternally inherited whole gene deletion of ALG11 in the patient.

evidence.reference_title: A recurrent c.953A>C (p. Gln318Pro) variant in ALG11 causing congenital disorder of glycosylation in Turkish population.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of two novel variants in ALG11 causing congenital disorder of glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Trio WES unveiled novel compound heterozygous variants: c.1307G>T (p.G436V) and c.1403G>A (p.R468H) within exon 4 of the ALG11 gene, inherited from the father and mother, respectively.

nodes.description: ALG11 activity is deficient at the fourth and fifth mannose-transfer steps of lipid-linked oligosaccharide assembly. The p.Leu86Ser index fibroblasts had impaired elongation despite unchanged measured protein abundance and localization. This catalytic phenotype should not be generalized to the abundance of every ALG11 variant.

nodes.description: Fibroblasts from two individuals homozygous for p.Pro311Leu or p.Thr55Ala were treated with 1 mM GLM101 for 24 hours in low-glucose culture and assessed by multiplexed proteomics and N-glycoproteomics. Some mature high-mannose glycopeptides increased, with a smaller response than in PMM2-CDG and ALG2-CDG. This is an experimental cellular intervention, not evidence of benefit in treated people.

nodes.description: In one molecularly and biochemically characterized child, fetal brain growth arrested after normal mid-gestation biometry. The fetal-to-neonatal MRI interval showed absent growth rather than measured tissue loss. The cellular mechanism connecting ALG11 dysfunction to this developmental phenotype is unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Arrest of Fetal Brain Development in ALG11-Congenital Disorder of Glycosylation.
evidence.snippet: During the 3.5 week interval from the fetal MRI to the postnatal brain MRI, the brain did not increase in size indicating an arrested growth pattern. This should be differentiated from a decrease in size, or atrophy, which did not occur during that same time period.

nodes.description: Serial MRI has documented progressive cerebral tissue loss in several severe cases. The child with prenatal growth arrest later had near-complete cerebral hemispheric loss and severe cerebellar and brainstem volume loss at age seven. That sequence is an individual longitudinal observation, not an obligatory course for all ALG11-CDG; another reported adolescent had normal MRI and CT.

nodes.description: Protein N-glycosylation is reduced. The index serum transferrin pattern reflected loss of complete N-glycan side chains, and affected fibroblasts show lower-molecular-weight GP130 glycoforms. These are protein- and sample-specific readouts: normal serum transferrin does not exclude a cellular defect. Comparative diagnostic sensitivity of GP130 versus transferrin has not been established.

nodes.description: Epilepsy was recorded in all 12 patients summarized in the 2019 phenotype review, commonly beginning in infancy. Drug resistance and status epilepticus occur, but the adolescent in that report had been seizure-free for seven years on medication. These selected reports do not define lifetime penetrance; the young fetal-onset case initially had no confirmed epilepsy.
